svg.aria-label: One edge drawn on two timelines: the reader clock in text offsets by chapter and the story clock in EDTF dates, with three example items
svg.text: Every edge carries when it is true in the story and where in the text the reader learns it. Two items as extracted from Hound ch. 1–3, and one placed to illustrate.
LOCATED_AT · Dr. James Mortimer → Charing Cross Hospital — revealed_pos 9,356 (ch 1) · story 1882/1884
“House-surgeon, from 1882 to 1884, at Charing Cross Hospital.” Both clocks known: the text states the years.
Fact · the legend of the hound — revealed in ch 2 · story date: none kept
The model proposed 1642 (from history) and 17XX (from the manuscript's date); neither is stated, voting dropped both as unstable.
IDENTICAL_TO · a late identity reveal — dashed and placed only to illustrate (the full-book graph holds one such edge)
Stage 2 keeps the two names apart; the edge would carry its own revealed_pos, so Spoilers-off cannot leak it.
WHAT THE SPOILERS CHECKBOX DOES TODAY
off → a character at chapter N may use items with revealed_pos ≤ the end of chapter N. A from ch 1; B from ch 2; C only after its reveal.
on → nothing is hidden by when the reader learns it. A real filter on the story clock would need a story date per chapter.
revealed_pos is set by code from the evidence quote. Story dates are model proposals that must quote a year and win 3 of 5 votes.
